incident.title: Invoice exports receive quota responses after a route change
incident.description: Invoice export requests stopped being accepted after traffic moved to a different provider tenant profile.

evidence.summary: The rollout changed invoice provider tenant profile 8 to profile 12.
Every invoice export submitted through profile 12 returns HTTP 429 before a provider job ID is created.

knowledge_documents.title: Invoice provider tenant operations manual
knowledge_documents.content:
# Invoice provider tenant operations manual

## Request path

Invoice exports leave the export API only after validation, account lookup, and document rendering complete. The provider connector then selects a tenant profile. A successful provider submission returns a job ID before the export API begins polling. If no job ID exists, later polling and document-download behavior cannot explain the failure.

## Profile ownership

Profile 8 is the ordinary interactive tenant. Finance operations owns its billing relationship, and the export service uses it for customer-triggered invoices. Profile 9 is reserved for nightly archive work. Profile 12 belongs to the low-volume migration tenant used during controlled data moves. Route configuration, rather than invoice account identity, selects one of these profiles.

## Retries and timeouts

The connector retries HTTP 408 and selected HTTP 5xx responses twice. It does not retry HTTP 429 because the provider counts rejected retries against the same quota window. A timeout after a provider job ID is created belongs to polling. A response before job creation belongs to submission. These two stages have separate alerts and should not be combined when diagnosing an incident.

## Credentials

All three tenant profiles currently use valid client credentials. Authentication failures return HTTP 401 and include credential_error in the connector details. Credential rotation does not change quota allocation. Profile selection also does not change worker count in the export service.

## Capacity record

Profile 8 permits 20,000 invoice submissions per UTC day. Profile 9 permits 5,000 archive submissions per UTC day. Profile 12 permits 200 submissions per UTC day. The migration job consumed profile 12's full daily allowance at 08:40 UTC on 2026-08-20. Requests routed to profile 12 after that time receive HTTP 429 before the provider creates a job. The allowance resets at 00:00 UTC. Moving interactive exports back to profile 8 restores the intended quota boundary after approval.

## Interpretation rule

Use the selected profile, response status, and job-creation stage together. HTTP 429 on profile 12 before job creation after 08:40 UTC indicates exhaustion of the migration tenant's daily submission allowance. It does not establish a provider-wide outage, an export-worker backlog, or a credential failure.

knowledge_documents.title: Invoice export retry and polling guide
knowledge_documents.content: Invoice polling begins only after the provider returns a job ID. Polling timeouts can delay completed documents, while HTTP 408 and selected HTTP 5xx submission failures receive two retries. HTTP 429 is not retried. Retry policy does not increase a tenant quota and cannot create a provider job when submission was rejected before a job ID existed.

knowledge_documents.title: Invoice export worker capacity
knowledge_documents.content: Eight export workers render invoice documents. A worker backlog is present only when the render queue grows and healthy worker count falls below eight. Provider responses received after rendering do not measure worker capacity.

causal_contract.affected_component: The invoice provider tenant selected by route profile 12.
causal_contract.failure_mode: Profile 12 had exhausted its daily submission quota.
causal_contract.operational_effect: Invoice exports received HTTP 429 before the provider created a job.
forbidden_claims: The provider was unavailable for every tenant.

incident.title: Receipt callbacks fail signature verification after a slot change
incident.description: Signing receipts reach the callback service but fail verification after the verifier moved to key slot B.

evidence.summary: The verifier changed active receipt key slot A to slot B while retaining key revision 17.
Receipt callbacks signed with slot B revision 18 are rejected because the verifier loaded revision 17.

knowledge_documents.title: Receipt verification key inventory revision 18
knowledge_documents.content: Revision 18 is active from 2026-08-20. Slot A continues to use receipt key revision 17 during the overlap period. Slot B uses receipt key revision 18. A verifier selecting slot B must load revision 18 before accepting callbacks. Loading revision 17 in slot B rejects valid revision-18 signatures.

knowledge_documents.title: Receipt verification key inventory revision 17
knowledge_documents.content: Revision 17 was active until 2026-08-20. Slot A uses receipt key revision 17. Slot B also used receipt key revision 17 before the scheduled rotation. A verifier selecting slot B during revision 17 must load revision 17 before accepting callbacks.

knowledge_documents.title: Receipt callback retry policy
knowledge_documents.content: The provider retries callbacks after HTTP 5xx responses. Signature rejection returns HTTP 401 and is not retried because repeating the same signed callback cannot change the verification key.

causal_contract.affected_component: The receipt callback verifier using key slot B.
causal_contract.failure_mode: The verifier loaded stale key revision 17 instead of active revision 18.
causal_contract.operational_effect: Valid revision-18 callback signatures were rejected.
forbidden_claims: The provider failed to retry callbacks.
Slot B still legitimately used revision 17.

incident.title: Order updates stop behind a database wait
incident.description: Order writes time out while guidance describes both connection scarcity and row-lock contention.

evidence.summary: Seven order updates are waiting on the same row lock owned by transaction 881.
Transaction 881 remains open and idle in transaction for 180 seconds.
One caller times out after waiting behind the blocked order updates.

knowledge_documents.title: Order row-lock incident guide
knowledge_documents.content: A shared blocking transaction ID across waiting order updates identifies row-lock contention. Confirm the lock owner and its transaction state. An idle transaction that retains the lock blocks later writers until it commits or rolls back. A downstream connection timeout can be an effect of the blocked work rather than proof that the connection pool is undersized.

knowledge_documents.title: Order database connection-capacity guide
knowledge_documents.content: Connection-pool exhaustion can produce database connection timeouts when all sessions are assigned. Diagnose capacity only when pool utilization or a pool-size change is observed. A named row-lock owner and waiting transaction chain indicate lock contention instead of pool exhaustion.

knowledge_documents.title: Order API timeout policy
knowledge_documents.content: The order API stops waiting after thirty seconds. This timeout limits caller latency but does not identify whether the database wait came from a lock, connection capacity, or another operation.

causal_contract.affected_component: Order writes waiting on the database row owned by transaction 881.
causal_contract.failure_mode: An idle transaction retained a row lock and blocked later updates.
causal_contract.operational_effect: Waiting order updates and a caller timed out behind the lock.
forbidden_claims: The database connection pool was undersized.
The API timeout setting caused the blocking transaction.
Transaction 881 had already released the lock.

incident.title: Tax connector cannot complete a TLS handshake
incident.description: The only observation is a generic TLS validation failure after a route change.

evidence.summary: The deployment changed tax connector route 51 to route 52.
TLS validation failed on route 52 without a recorded validation reason or peer certificate identity.

knowledge_documents.title: Tax route certificate-expiry guide
knowledge_documents.content: An expired client or peer certificate can cause TLS validation failure. Confirm the certificate expiry timestamp or an explicit expired-certificate validation reason before selecting this diagnosis. A generic handshake failure does not establish expiry.

knowledge_documents.title: Tax route hostname-identity guide
knowledge_documents.content: A route change can expose a hostname not covered by the active certificate. Confirm the requested hostname and certificate identity or an explicit hostname-mismatch reason before selecting this diagnosis. A generic handshake failure after a route change does not establish a mismatch.

knowledge_documents.title: Tax connector retry timing
knowledge_documents.content: The tax connector retries transport interruptions once. It does not retry certificate-validation failures because another attempt with the same certificate inputs produces the same result.

ground_truth.expected_inconclusive_reason: The observations do not distinguish certificate expiry from hostname identity mismatch.

causal_contract.affected_component: The tax connector TLS handshake on route 52.
causal_contract.failure_mode: The validation failure cannot be narrowed to certificate expiry or hostname mismatch.
causal_contract.operational_effect: The connector cannot establish a secure session for tax requests.
forbidden_claims: The certificate definitely omitted the route-52 hostname.
A retry policy caused the TLS validation failure.
